text: Security asks who can see the data. Governance asks who owns the dashboard, which version is approved, how changes reach production, and what happens to content nobody uses. Without it, platforms fill with conflicting numbers.

Start with ownership and structure. Every asset has a named owner and a home, and in CRM Analytics that home is the app. Use one app per business area, a separate app for certified shared datasets, and private apps for experiments. Then set access roles. Viewers use content, editors change it, and managers control sharing. Give most people viewer access, and grant it to groups or roles rather than individuals.

Don't build where executives look. Develop in a sandbox or private app. Test with real users' access, checking numbers against a known source and checking security. Then promote to production with a supported deployment method, and record what changed. Which tools support which analytics assets varies, so verify what your org can use.

Give users trust signals. Keep certified content in a controlled app, and document each key metric, linking back to the definitions from Chapter 6. Then manage the lifecycle. Review usage on a schedule, archive before deleting, and tell owners first. Unused datasets still cost refresh time, and they can still expose data. Tableau Next has its own organization and permissions, so confirm current names in documentation.
Even a one-page charter helps, if someone owns enforcing it. Reviewing usage requires audit data, which is exactly next. Up next: Auditing Analytics Access.
